reply.subject: RM_ModernBridge_winches

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South and north are mirror images of the same chain-drum winch: a dark blue-grey steel base frame with two uprights holding a drum wound with dark chain, and a gearbox/motor on one side (right on south, left on north). East is a different-looking assembly: a beige concrete housing with a louvred vent, an amber lamp and a door panel, a steel hood with a yellow dashed stripe on top, and the chain drum seen end-on with two chain strands running out to the right. All steel trim is a cool dark slate grey. There is no red anywhere.
observed.south.png: Winch seen from the front, slightly from above. Light steel flanges on the drum, a black chain coil, a grey gearbox with bolted covers and a finned motor end, and a dark slate-grey I-beam base with bolted foot pads. The top faces of the base and the gearbox are lit and visible but shallow. Clean alpha with no ground patch.
observed.east.png: Side view: a concrete plinth and housing on the left with a small elbow pipe stub, vent grille, amber indicator and door. A dark slate-grey steel hood over the drum carries a yellow dashed line on its lit top face. The chain drum shows inside, with two chain runs leaving east. The hood's top face is visible. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Mirror of south: drum on the right, gearbox and motor on the left, same dark grey steel base, same chain. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: On a 2x2-ish footprint outline beside a vanilla human. The winch is roughly human-height and fills its outlined footprint, with the side shaft ends slightly outside it. At 32 px/cell the chain drum and grey frame still read as a winch.
observed.variants_1.png: Timber kind of the same family: a wooden frame on a plank base with dark iron brackets, a rope drum and a crank handle, shown front and side. The wood is brown and the iron dark grey. No red.
observed.assembled_1.png: Offline composite: a long light-grey galvanised/steel-plank deck spanning grey water between brown riverbank strips, with dark slate-grey riveted edge rails. The winch sits at the upper-left corner, overlapping the deck edge rail, and draws over the deck. The whole scene reads grey and steel, with no plumbing red or blue accents.

CAMERA.seen: Building camera from slightly above, with lit top faces on the base, gearbox and the east hood. The shape and perspective are pixel-identical to the kept art and out of scope for this recolour.

LAYERS.seen: In assembled_1 the winch draws over the deck edge rail and deck, which is correct for a building standing on the deck corner. Nothing behind it draws over it.

ROTATIONS.seen: The palette is consistent on every facing: the same dark slate-grey steel, light steel flanges and dark chain. East's concrete housing differs in form from south/north, but form is kept art and out of scope. The colour treatment agrees across facings.

SIGNATURE.seen: The chain drum, gearbox/motor and anchored base frame read as a drawbridge winch. The Timber variant is a rope drum with a crank.

MATERIAL.seen: The blue-grey reads as painted structural steel (highway-bridge style), as intended. Flanges and gearbox read as machined metal and the east plinth as concrete. The chain reads as dark iron.

FOOTPRINT.seen: In scale.png it fills its outlined footprint, with only the drum shaft ends slightly past the sides. The code measures cross-facing height spread at 6%.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on every facing with no backdrop, halo or ground shadow, as the code also measured.

OURS.seen: This is the kept RimMandrake art, recoloured. It is not a donor sprite.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The firetruck red is gone. The steel is dark blue-grey bridge steel and nothing reads as water plumbing (no red/blue hydrant colours). The assembled view reads as a modern steel bridge.

LEGIBLE.seen: In the 32 px/cell inset of scale.png the dark drum and grey frame still read as a winch.
